page: Microsoft Azure L4s_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz, configured with 4 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU configuration includes a 260 MB L3 cache alongside support for advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). Memory capacity is 32.0 GB, yielding a high memory allocation ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware resources include a bundled 960 GB local NVMe solid-state drive, while graphics processing units are not included.

Benchmark results highlight solid single-thread compute capabilities, driven by the 4.2 GHz clock rate and instruction support. The instance records a strong Geekbench single-core score of 2158.0 and gzip compression throughput of 31.48 GB/sec. Text processing workloads also register in the upper quartile at 2551.0 points. In contrast, multi-threaded capacity reflects the physical constraint of 2 underlying cores, resulting in lower scores on multi-core stress-ng tests (3990.37) and software compilation tasks. Memory bandwidth tests demonstrate moderate performance, measuring 36.35 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 25.49 GB/sec for writes.

Given the balanced allocation of 8.0 GB RAM per vCPU and fast attached NVMe storage, the L4s_v4 provides an efficient resource footprint for I/O-intensive workloads without incurring excessive multi-core compute overhead. It exhibits sufficient throughput for static web serving (7.76 GB/sec) and handles small-scale language model inference effectively, though larger parameter models reveal CPU computation bottlenecks. Best-fit use cases include operational relational databases, caching layers, NoSQL stores, and data ingestion pipelines requiring rapid local scratch space.
description: Microsoft Azure L4s_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs (2 physical cores) powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz with 260 MB L3 cache, AVX-512, and AMX support. The system delivers 32.0 GB of memory (8.0 GB per core) and includes a dedicated 960 GB local NVMe SSD without discrete GPUs. In synthetic testing, the instance exhibits strong single-threaded CPU execution with a Geekbench single-core score of 2158.0 and rapid gzip compression of 31.48 GB/sec. However, multi-threaded throughput and memory bandwidth reflect its compact core count, as seen in stress-ng multi-core and larger LLM inference benchmarks. With its dense memory-to-core ratio and direct NVMe storage, the L4s_v4 is well suited for database operations, I/O-sensitive caching layers, and lightweight transaction processing.
